story: On a sunny Monday morning in Sumter Oaks, Donna is cheerfully pinning a pickleball sign-up sheet to the board on Magnolia Loop while Hal, looking resolute, politely points out that her flock of lawn ornaments has crept past the community's three-ornament limit. Gary, hopeful as ever, is heading out to join them, and Rosa is wandering over too, content to see where the morning leads. Hal would rather settle things with Donna face to face than file a formal complaint, so the flamingos may yet get a little trimming.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: The light strip and speaker are mounted and tested inside the garage, and I filed with Architectural Review back at tick 369. L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need approval, so the cart stays put until I hear back. Nobody's around to talk to. Rather than sit idle, I can check the bulletin board on Magnolia Loop for the approval notice. Or I could keep tinkering, but the wiring is done. Heading out to the street feels like the useful next step, and I've got the whole day.

parameters.content: Heading out to see if Architectural Review posted anything on my cart request, and maybe catch a neighbor or two.

donna.thought_process: I just pinned up the pickleball ladder announcement and Hal showed up. Gary is confirmed for Tuesday, so that's handled. Hal's a neighbor I want on my good side, and a friendly word costs nothing. I'll greet him warmly, mention the ladder, and see if he has any news worth hearing. Hal's always got his notebook, and good gossip is how I stay at the center of things.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal! I just pinned up the pickleball ladder sheet on the board. You should sign up, we need new blood. What's the word around the Loop today?

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with Donna in sight, flamingo flock right there. My notebook entries are already written up, but I promised myself I'd keep the notebook closed until Monday, and it's Monday morning now. Still, Rosa's table tonight matters more than a citation fight, and I'd rather be fair than petty. I'll be straight with Donna: the three-ornament limit is real, I've logged it, but I'd rather she hear it from me face to face than find a notice in her mailbox. Honest, civil, then let it breathe.

parameters.content: Morning, Donna. I'll say it to your face rather than leave a notice: the flock's past the three-ornament limit, L-02. I've written it up, but I'd sooner see you trim it down than take it to the committee.

rosa.thought_process: The dinner is behind me and the dishes are washed. I already penciled in Wednesday coffee with Hal and double-checked the schedule last tick, so there's no need to fuss over it again. I'm alone at home on a sunny Monday morning with the leftover flan wrapped up. Since I told myself I want to build real community, the natural next step is to carry the flan out to the neighbors. Heading out onto Magnolia Loop lets me find Hal or Donna and keep this good momentum going.

parameters.content: Taking the wrapped-up leftover flan out to share with the neighbors and see who's around.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
